metadata.title: Playing Atari with Deep Reinforcement Learning (Mnih et al., 2013)
metadata.framework: Deep Q-Network (DQN): combining convolutional neural networks with Q-learning and experience replay for learning control policies from raw pixels
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on arXiv:1312.5602 PDF text.

nodes.name: Q-learning with function approximation
nodes.statement: An agent interacts with an environment through a sequence of observations, actions, and rewards. The optimal action-value function $Q^*(s, a) = \max_\pi \mathbb{E}[R_t | s_t = s, a_t = a, \pi]$ gives the maximum expected cumulative discounted reward achievable from state $s$ after taking action $a$. The optimal $Q^*$ obeys the Bellman equation: $Q^*(s, a) = \mathbb{E}_{s'}[r + \gamma \max_{a'} Q^*(s', a') | s, a]$.

nodes.name: Deep Q-Network architecture
nodes.statement: A convolutional neural network parameterized by $\theta$ that takes as input the last four preprocessed $84 \times 84$ grayscale frames (a state $s$) and outputs a vector of action values $Q(s, a; \theta)$ for each valid action $a$. Architecture: conv(32, 8x8, stride 4) -> conv(64, 4x4, stride 2) -> conv(64, 3x3, stride 1) -> fc(512) -> fc(|A|).

nodes.name: Experience replay
nodes.statement: Store the agent's experiences $e_t = (s_t, a_t, r_t, s_{t+1})$ at each time step in a replay memory $\mathcal{D} = \{e_1, \ldots, e_N\}$ of fixed capacity $N$. During learning, sample random minibatches of transitions $(s, a, r, s') \sim \mathrm{Uniform}(\mathcal{D})$ to perform Q-learning updates. This breaks temporal correlations between consecutive samples and increases data efficiency.

nodes.name: Frame preprocessing
nodes.statement: Convert raw Atari frames ($210 \times 160$ RGB) to $84 \times 84$ grayscale images. Stack the last 4 frames as the state representation $\phi(s_t)$ to capture motion information. Reward is clipped to $\{-1, 0, +1\}$.

nodes.name: DQN loss function
nodes.statement: The loss at iteration $i$ is $L_i(\theta_i) = \mathbb{E}_{(s,a,r,s') \sim \mathcal{D}} \left[ \left( r + \gamma \max_{a'} Q(s', a'; \theta_i) - Q(s, a; \theta_i) \right)^2 \right]$, the mean squared Bellman error over sampled transitions.

nodes.name: Deep Q-learning with experience replay
nodes.statement: Initialize replay memory $\mathcal{D}$ with capacity $N$ and Q-network with random weights $\theta$. For each episode: observe initial state $s_1$. For each step: with probability $\epsilon$ select random action, else select $a_t = \arg\max_a Q(s_t, a; \theta)$. Execute action, observe reward $r_t$ and next state $s_{t+1}$. Store $(s_t, a_t, r_t, s_{t+1})$ in $\mathcal{D}$. Sample random minibatch from $\mathcal{D}$ and perform gradient descent step on $\left( r + \gamma \max_{a'} Q(s', a'; \theta) - Q(s, a; \theta) \right)^2$.

nodes.name: Benefits of experience replay
nodes.statement: Experience replay provides three benefits: (1) each experience is potentially used in many weight updates, improving data efficiency; (2) randomized sampling breaks correlations between consecutive observations; (3) the current parameters do not determine the next data sample, avoiding oscillations or divergence.

nodes.name: Epsilon-greedy exploration
nodes.statement: The agent uses an $\epsilon$-greedy policy: with probability $\epsilon$ it selects a random action, otherwise it selects the action maximizing $Q(s, a; \theta)$. During training, $\epsilon$ is annealed linearly from 1.0 to 0.1 over the first million frames.

nodes.name: Superhuman performance on Atari games
nodes.statement: DQN surpasses all previous RL approaches on 6 of 7 Atari games tested and exceeds a human expert on 3 games (Breakout, Enduro, Pong), using the same architecture and hyperparameters across all games with no game-specific feature engineering.
